thread:
incident-bot: ALERT P0 — warmup error spike on gpu-pool-alpha: multiple model-warmup OOMs + compile-timeouts detected for redwood-7b-q. 120s error rate > 25%

sam (oncall): I'm picking this up. seeing a burst of OOMs across 3 nodes, starting ~1723456720.

maria (eng-runtime): copying logs: `grep -i "OOM|deserialize|compile timeout" /var/log/warmup/last-15m.log` shows repeated:
```
E OOM allocating 1.2GB during weight deserialization
E compile timeout: kernel selection timed out after 30s
E cudart: device-side assert in cuModuleLoad
```

jordan (eng-sre): node health: gpu-pool-alpha-{3,4,7} flapped, pods restarted 2x. Memory pressure + eviction churn.

sam (oncall): impact? any customer-facing errors?

linda (support): Support telemetry shows ~18k requests retried, ~220 errors surfaced to customers (mostly embeddings). Two enterprise customers reported degraded throughput.

kevin (eng-ml): model variant redwood-7b-q quantized build was onlining with compile-cache enabled — might be hitting a pathological compile path.

maria (eng-runtime): mitigation ideas: 1) disable compile cache on warmup 2) pause parallel warmups for this model 3) route new warmups to dedicated cold-pool (cpu fallback) 4) restart affected nodes if kernel panics persist. Thoughts?

sam (oncall): do first two immediately. jordan, can you disable parallel warmup policy for redwood-7b-q in routing layer?

jordan (eng-sre): on it: `curl -X POST https://router.internal/disable_warmup -d '{"model":"redwood-7b-q","parallel":false}'` -> 202 accepted.

maria (eng-runtime): turning off compile-cache on the controller for the model: `PATCH /models/redwood-7b-q/config {"compile_cache":false}` -> applying to 3 regions. Pushing now.

incident-bot: NOTE — change recorded by maria (eng-runtime) at 1723456775.

sam (oncall): we're also going to throttle new warmup traffic for the pool and reject low-priority warmups. jordan, please bump eviction threshold slightly to avoid churn.

jordan (eng-sre): bumped eviction headroom +10% on gpu-pool-alpha. node restarts queued for node-7 which has repeated cudart panics.

linda (support): telling affected customers: "We've identified a transient warmup regression affecting a small subset of GPU-backed models. We've applied mitigations and are monitoring. No data was lost; some requests saw retries or temporary latency increases." Planning to send an update in 30m.

kevin (eng-ml): quick note — if compile timeouts were caused by specific opcode patterns, disabling compile cache will avoid repeated heavy compilation attempts. Good call. We should add a guard to not compile >2 concurrent kernels per model.

maria (eng-runtime): stats: post-mitigations error rate down from 27% -> 4% in the last 3m. OOMs reduced but node-7 still shows kernel panics; team recommends cordon/drain+recreate.

sam (oncall): Jordan, please cordon node-7 and rotate workloads. Maria, keep watch on warmup queue and re-enable progressive warmup after 30m if stable.

jordan (eng-sre): node-7 cordoned and drained. Recreation initiated.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigations applied (compile_cache off, parallel warmups paused, eviction headroom increased, node-7 drained). Customer impact reduced.

linda (support): posting interim status to customers now.

sam (oncall): handing off to eng-runtime for postmortem and follow-ups. I'll remain available. tagging @maria for lead.

maria (eng-runtime): ack — we'll run a targeted postmortem and include: root cause (compile-cache + quantized warmup pattern), mitigation playbook additions, and a guard to limit concurrent kernel compiles. Will file PM and link to this thread.

kevin (eng-ml): assigning a follow-up to investigate whether model artifact serialization has edge cases that increase memory during deserialization.

incident-bot: HANDOFF from oncall sam to eng-runtime maria at 1723456820.

sam (oncall): closing active page. Will mark incident P0->P1 in pagerduty after eng-runtime confirms stability. Good work team :thumbsup:"
